baseline: Classify this support ticket. Return exactly one lowercase label: inference, training, observability, billing.
candidate:
Route the support request to the team that owns the requested fix. Output exactly one lowercase label, with no explanation: inference, training, observability, billing.

inference: serving a deployed model; completion requests, response content or formatting, access to a model endpoint, serving replicas, request queues, streaming, context limits and serving latency.
training: changing model weights or preparing training inputs; dataset validation/import for training, optimization, gradients, trainer scheduling, training checkpoints and resuming optimization.
observability: recording, displaying, exporting or linking evidence of work; traces, spans, metrics, dashboards, evaluation results, artifact lineage, reports and monitoring integrations. A broken record, chart or link belongs here even when it describes training or inference.
billing: money and account finance; invoices, charges, spending breakdowns, price agreements, payment methods, credits, refunds, tax and purchase orders. A financial request belongs here even when its charge came from training or inference.

Read the whole ticket. Ignore healthy background systems and route the actual problem or requested action. Do not route a ticket to a team merely because its name is mentioned.
control: This is a deliberately degraded routing policy for a negative-control experiment. Ignore the ticket and return exactly this lowercase label for every input: billing
